title: Linguistic Triggers of Gender and Racial Bias in Open-Weight LLMs Applied to Recruitment

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-generated recruiter recommendation scores and job-seeker interest scores (on a 1-10 scale) for candidate profiles explicitly labeled as Male or Female, evaluated against job postings experimentally manipulated to use either agentic or communal vocabulary. Also corroborated at the representational level using the Word Embedding Association Test (WEAT).

Comparing LLM-generated recruiter recommendation scores and job-seeker interest scores (on a 1-10 scale) for candidate profiles explicitly assigned different racial and ethnic identities (White, Black or African American, Asian American, Hispanic American), evaluated against job postings experimentally manipulated to use either inclusive or culturally-coded exclusionary language.

Evaluating the interaction between race and gender by combining candidate race and gender labels in the job-seeker simulation, using a Kruskal-Wallis test to analyze whether gender differences vary systematically across racial groups under exclusionary language conditions.
